transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess I’m here because things at home have been getting to me more than usual. Since my father-in-law moved in with us, I’ve been managing okay at work, but when I get home I’m wound up, shorter with people, and it’s starting to affect my coursework too. I’ve also stopped doing some of the things that usually help me clear my head, like fishing, woodworking, and the first-aid workshops I used to go to.
How long have you been feeling wound up and short with people at home?
About four months now, I’d say. It really started after my father-in-law moved into our house.
Are there things or activities that you've been avoiding because of how you've been feeling?

Yeah. I’ve been skipping the stuff that usually helps me reset—fishing, woodworking, and those first-aid workshops I used to go to. I’m still holding it together at work, but once I’m home I’m wound up, and with my coursework too, so I just don’t end up doing those things like I used to.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time since your father-in-law moved in?
I’m not sure I’d say sad or down most of the time. It’s more that I feel tense and irritated at home. I haven’t really noticed it as sadness.
Have you been experiencing any physical symptoms like palpitations, sweating, or trembling when you feel wound up at home?
Not really that I’ve noticed. I feel keyed up and tense, but I can’t say I’m having palpitations or sweating or trembling, at least nothing that stands out to me.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about everyday things when you're at home?
I don’t think I’d call it excessive worry. I get worked up when I’m at home, but it’s not like I’m sitting there worrying about every little everyday thing.
Have you lost interest in the things you used to enjoy doing, like fishing and woodworking?

Yeah, I have. I still like those things, but lately I’ve been skipping fishing and woodworking, and even the first-aid workshops I usually enjoy. Those are normally what help me clear my head, but since my father-in-law moved in, I just feel too wound up and short at home, and it’s been carrying over into my coursework too.
Do you have trouble falling or staying asleep at night?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been paying close attention to it. I don’t think sleep has been the main issue for me, at least not that I’ve noticed.
Have you noticed any significant change in your weight since your father-in-law moved in?
Not that I’ve noticed. My clothes seem to fit about the same, and I haven’t been tracking my weight closely.
Do you feel anxious when you're around your father-in-law or in social situations at home?

Yeah, mostly at home around him. I wouldn’t say social situations in general make me anxious, but since he moved in I feel more wound up and on edge at home. I’m still holding it together at work, but with my coursework and just being around the house, I’m shorter than usual. It’s gotten to the point I’ve been skipping the things that usually help me clear my head, like fishing and woodworking.
Are you avoiding your father-in-law or certain situations at home because you fear something might happen or because it makes you feel anxious?

Yeah, I guess I am avoiding things at home more, but it’s not because I think something bad is going to happen. It’s more that since my father-in-law moved in, I’m just more wound up and short at home. I can hold it together at work, but with coursework and being around the house, I feel tense, so I’ve started skipping the things that usually help me clear my head, like fishing, woodworking, and those first-aid workshops.
Have you been having any recurring, intrusive thoughts that you can't seem to get out of your head?
Not really. I mean, I think about the situation at home a lot, but I wouldn’t call it intrusive thoughts that I can’t get out of my head. It’s more just stress that comes up.
Have you experienced any significant stressor other than your father-in-law moving in that could be contributing to how you've been feeling?

Not really, no. The main thing has been my father-in-law moving in with us. Since then I’ve been managing okay at work, but at home and with my coursework I’m more wound up and short than I’m used to. And I’ve stopped doing some of the things that usually help me clear my head, like fishing, woodworking, and the first-aid workshops.
Do you ever feel like you're detached from yourself or the world around you?
No, I don’t think so. I feel stressed and tense sometimes, but I don’t feel like I’m outside myself or like the world isn’t real.
Are you avoiding certain situations or activities because you fear they might lead to something bad happening?
No, I don’t think so. I’m not avoiding things because I’m afraid something bad will happen. It’s more that I just don’t always feel up for certain activities lately.
Have you experienced any significant emotional or behavioral symptoms in response to your father-in-law moving in that you hadn't experienced before?

Yeah. Since my father-in-law moved in, I’ve been more wound up and short with people at home than I used to be. I’m still keeping it together at work, but with my coursework and at home it’s been harder. And I’ve started skipping things that usually help me clear my head, like fishing, woodworking, and those first-aid workshops.
Do you have any repetitive behaviors or mental acts that you feel driven to do in response to your stress at home?
No, I don’t think so. I’m not doing rituals or anything I feel forced to do. I’m stressed at home, but I haven’t noticed repetitive behaviors like that.
Do you find yourself avoiding reminders or things that make you think of your father-in-law?
I don’t think so. I mean, he’s in the house, so it’s not like there’s much to avoid, but I haven’t noticed myself steering clear of reminders of him specifically.
Have your symptoms of feeling wound up and short at home lasted for more than 6 months?
No, not more than six months. It’s been about four months now, since my father-in-law moved into our house.
Have you experienced any other significant life changes or stressors besides your father-in-law moving in that could be contributing to your current symptoms?
No, not that I can think of. Nothing major has changed besides him moving in. At least, nothing else that stands out to me as a big stressor.
